subject: Snowbridge: intermittent large-upload failures - egress fragmentation & SG check
messages:
From: Tim Nguyen <tim.nguyen@snowbridge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Snowbridge NOC <noc@snowbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Uploads failing intermittently to private deployment (large files)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent failures from our on-prem clients to the Redwood Private front-end. Symptoms:
- Uploads > ~64KB frequently get TCP RST / connection reset after ~100-130s.
- Smaller requests succeed.
- Problem started after a firewall firmware update on our edge (FortiOS).

I've attached a pcap from one failed upload (snowbridge_capture_20261218.pcap) and an MTU check (mtu-test-results.txt). Host MTU shows 1500; traceroute + path MTU tests indicate a hop dropping packets > ~1420. Firewall logs show a MSS clamp entry around 1380.

Can you confirm if there's anything on the Redwood Private side that would cause fragmentation or SNAT-related asymmetry? This is impacting a production batch job. Appreciate quick help.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Nguyen
SRE Lead, Snowbridge Health
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: snowbridge_capture_20261218.pcap (pcap), mtu-test-results.txt (text)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tim Nguyen <tim.nguyen@snowbridge.com>, Snowbridge NOC <noc@snowbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uploads failing intermittently to private deployment (large files)

Thanks for the data, Tim — looking through the pcap now. Quick ack and next steps so we can isolate: 

1) Can you run these on one of the affected on-prem hosts and paste results?
   - sudo tcpdump -i <app_iface> -s0 -w /tmp/out.pcap host <private-frontdoor-ip>
   - iperf3 -c <private-frontdoor-ip> -t 30 -P 1
   - ping -M do -s 1400 <private-frontdoor-ip> && ping -M do -s 1420 <private-frontdoor-ip>
   - curl --trace-time -v -F file=@largefile.bin https://<private-frontdoor-host>/upload

2) Does your FortiGate have an MSS-clamp or DF-bit rewrite policy? The MSS clamp reported in your logs is suspicious. If you can share the exact firewall rule text that was changed in the recent firmware upgrade, that helps.

3) On the Redwood side we will check:
   - whether the customer route is being SNATed twice (edge device + private egress).
   - host NIC offload (GRO/LRO) interactions that cause large frames to be coalesced and then mismatched checksums on middleboxes.
   - our health-check/security-group config to ensure the health probes aren't being dropped (you mentioned some missing health checks).

Please run the tests above and attach the tcpdump (full pcap) and iperf output. I'll loop in Dylan and Laura for kernel/offload and SG checks.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: Tim Nguyen <tim.nguyen@snowbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Snowbridge escalation: egress fragmentation + possible double-SNAT + SG health-check drops

Team — summarizing and proposed mitigation path. Customer data shows:
- FortiGate is clamping MSS to 1380 post-upgrade. When they temporarily lowered clamp to 1200, uploads succeeded.
- Path MTU to the private frontdoor crosses a hop that will not forward larger packets (PMTU ~1420).
- There are signs of SNAT happening at customer edge and again at our private egress IP (double SNAT) which leads to asymmetric flows and conntrack misses when packets get fragmented.
- Health-check denies look like an outbound SG rule on their side blocking our health probe IP (we get a deny for probe IP x.x.x.x).

Immediate mitigation options (pick a short/medium/long plan):
* Short (0-4h): Request Snowbridge NOC to temporarily set FortiGate MSS clamp to 1360 and open an ACL to allow our health-check IPs (443 + TCP probes). This is the fastest way to validate frag vs. SNAT.
* Medium (4-24h): Route Snowbridge traffic via an alternate SNAT pool on our side (bypass their edge SNAT path) to avoid double SNAT asymmetry; requires change in Private routing policy + NAT rule. Can be reversed quickly.
* Long (>24h): Work with Snowbridge to remove DF rewrite / MSS-clamp at firewall and ensure P-TCP MSS negotiation is preserved, and tune kernel offload parameters on their hosts (disable GRO/LRO as a test).

Requests:
- Dylan: please review host NIC offload interactions and whether our frontdoor handles fragmented packets or relies on PMTU. Provide a checklist to disable GRO/LRO for test.
- Laura: confirm whether our Private egress is performing SNAT for this tenant and whether we can spin a temporary non-SNAT path.
- Marissa: please prepare an ops playbook and rollback plan for the medium mitigation (route to alternate SNAT). Include expected impact and required maintenance window.

I am looping the customer for permission to run short maintenance (5-10 minutes) and to apply the short mitigation first (MSS->1360 + health-check whitelist).

-Karthik

1) I've opened RED-7891 with infra and Private Deploy ops and pasted packet excerpts + the FortiGate rule text.
2) Infra confirms our private egress currently SNATs Snowbridge connections to pool 10.200.45.0/27. We can provision a temporary non-SNAT route for this tenant — low risk and reversible.
3) I'll coordinate an emergency 30-minute maintenance window with Snowbridge NOC tonight PST. Plan:
   - Snowbridge will set MSS clamp to 1360 for 30 minutes and whitelist our health-check IP (x.x.x.x).
   - We provision alternate route that keeps original source IP (no SNAT) for the duration.
   - We will run controlled uploads and capture pcaps on both sides (customer and our frontdoor).

If the controlled test confirms the hypothesis (uploads succeed under lower MSS + no SNAT), we recommend the following permanent steps:
- Snowbridge: revert FortiGate MSS clamp to preserve MSS negotiation (or set to 1360 as a safe default if vendor insists on clamp).
- Snowbridge: ensure DF/DF-rewrite is not enforced; preserve PMTU discoveries.
- Redwood: add detection for double-SNAT in our Private console (alert when same tenant appears SNATed by customer IP and our egress).

Marissa — please prepare the playbook and the change ticket for RED-7891 so we can get approvals during the window. Laura — once infra has the non-SNAT route ready, send me the CIDR and I'll include it in the ticket.

Dylan
